newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends at record bourse high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends at record bourse high.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares closeed floor trade at a record high on Friday, driven by gains in bond prices and by the Dow Jones index which ended overnight above 6,200 points for first time.
The DAX raced up to a day high of 2,744.90 points and then slipped back slightly to end up 26.61 points, or 0.98 percent, at 2,739.83, a new record bourse close.
The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day computer dealings in the DAX, did not manage to hold onto its record high level of 2,745.84 and ended trade at 2,732.29 points, up 8.04 points.
The DAX suffered in electronic trade as Wall Street opened lower and the dollar weakened below 1.51 marks, seen as negative for German exporters.

Meanwhile shares in dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care dropped 2.5 two percent against the firmer market trend, falling 3.50 marks to 136.50 marks in IBIS dealings, after the company reported nine month sales of $2.3 billion against $2.1 billion a year previously.
Dealers said although the results were in line with analysts' expectations, the market had come to demand outperformance from the group.

Diversified industrial group Viag AG climbed ahead of the trend, gaining 7.65 marks to 585.20 marks in electronic trade, after the firm said nine month group sales were unchanged at about 32 billion marks.
The company also said it expected 1996 group pretax profit to be at least as high as in 1995.
But shares in Viag subsidiary, speciality chemicals group SKW Trostberg, fell almost nine percent to hit a low of 40.90 marks, despite Viag saying sales increased at the unit.

The main selling on the stock came after BHF bank cut its recommendations on the firm to a "hold" from a "buy" and reduced its earnings per share estimates, saying the firm's results had been "slightly disappointing."
But the stock recovered somewhat to end IBIS trade at 43.30 marks, down 1.70 marks, after Paribas Capital Markets said it was maintaining its "buy" on the stock.
Shares in Dresdner Bank AG reached an all-time IBIS high of 43.19 marks and closed computer dealings up 1.23 marks at 42.75 marks.

Dealers said the stock reacted positively to news that the bank planned to merge its global funds businesses and was also boosted as investors, including Salomon Brothers, reiterated "buy" recommendations on the stock.
